method: Each scenario builds labelled synthetic data (stored as simulated_baseline: Ring event shape, not Ring-originated), runs the real ingestion, correlation, funnel, pattern and analyst code, then compares the behaviour with the stated expectation. Every scenario runs in a transaction that is rolled back.

scenarios.title: Activity and sales remain steady
scenarios.detail: no pattern is flagged and the decline premise is reported as not supported

scenarios.title: Probable test-drive activity rises while sales fall
scenarios.expectation: Flag the pattern and show its evidence
scenarios.detail: the pattern is flagged with the counts behind it

scenarios.title: One comparison period has missing data
scenarios.expectation: Explain the gap and withhold unsupported conclusions

observed.reason: One period has no visits or no probable test-drive sessions, so a conversion rate cannot be compared.

scenarios.detail: the verdict is withheld and names what is missing

scenarios.title: Several departures could match a return
scenarios.expectation: Show that the result depends on the matching assumption
scenarios.detail: the session count changes with the matching window, so the result is shown as assumption-dependent

scenarios.title: Bedrock is unavailable

observed.summary: These metrics describe what changed at this dealership between the two periods. They do not prove a cause.

scenarios.detail: a labelled deterministic fallback is returned, with no invented figures

scenarios.title: The model's answer contradicts the figures it cites
scenarios.expectation: Reject the answer on meaning, not just on shape

observed.error: answer rejected: summary contradicts sales_conversion.change_points, which shows no material change
observed.summary: These metrics describe what changed at this dealership between the two periods. They do not prove a cause.

scenarios.detail: the answer is rejected for contradicting the figures and the labelled fallback is shown
